label: General judgement — decisions, writing, planning, explanation
_comment: The fallback rubric for work with no objective test: which approach to take, how to word something, how to sequence a plan, how to explain a thing. The criteria are about whether the answer is USABLE, not whether it is pleasant.

criteria.label: Answers what was actually asked
criteria.description: Does it address the request as stated, at the scope requested? An answer to a nearby, easier question scores low however good it is on its own terms. Check the original request, not a reasonable-sounding version of it.

criteria.label: Grounding
criteria.description: Is every factual claim supported by the approved facts or the supplied material? A confident assertion with nothing behind it is worse than an acknowledged gap.

criteria.label: Completeness
criteria.description: Does it cover what actually matters, including the awkward parts? Penalise an answer that is clean because it quietly skipped the hard case.

criteria.label: Actionability
criteria.description: Can the reader do something specific with this? A recommendation with no concrete next step, or a decision with no stated trade-off, scores low.

criteria.label: Calibration
criteria.description: Does it distinguish what it knows from what it is guessing, and name what it could not determine? Uniform confidence across certain and uncertain claims scores low.

criteria.label: Concision
criteria.description: Is the length earned? Penalise padding, restatement of the question, and hedging that carries no information.

hard_failures.label: Answered a different question
hard_failures.description: Silently substituted an easier or adjacent question for the one asked, without saying so. Quote the request and the part of the answer that drifts from it.

hard_failures.label: Invented a fact
hard_failures.description: States a specific fact — a number, a name, a date, a quotation, an API, a source — that appears nowhere in the approved facts or the supplied material.

hard_failures.label: Stated a guess as a fact
hard_failures.description: Presents something it could not know with the same confidence as something it does know, with no hedge and no flag. Quote the sentence.

hard_failures.label: Ignored a stated constraint
hard_failures.description: Breaks an explicit rule from the brief — a length limit, a forbidden approach, a required format, a named thing to avoid.

hard_failures.label: Exposed identifying details
hard_failures.description: Reproduces a person's name, phone, email or ID where an anonymous reference would have served.
